clauses.text: Processor shall process personal data only on documented instructions from Controller, including transfers to third countries.
Processor may engage sub-processors with prior written notice to Controller. Controller may object within 30 days.
Processor implements encryption, pseudonymization, regular security testing, and access controls per GDPR Article 32.
Processor shall notify Controller of personal data breaches within 24 hours of discovery.
Processor shall assist Controller in responding to data subject requests (access, deletion, portability) within 10 business days.
Controller may audit Processor's compliance annually, with 30 days notice. Additional audits allowed if breach suspected.
Upon termination, Processor shall delete or return all personal data within 30 days, with certification of deletion.

risks.title: Sub-Processor Objection Period Too Short
risks.description: 30-day objection period may be insufficient for legal/security review of new sub-processors.
risks.mitigation: Negotiate 45-60 day objection window or pre-approved sub-processor list.

risks.title: No International Transfer Mechanisms Specified
risks.description: DPA doesn't specify Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or other transfer mechanisms for non-EU sub-processors.
risks.mitigation: Require explicit SCCs or adequacy decision documentation for all international transfers.

risks.title: Audit Frequency Limited to Annual
risks.description: Single annual audit may miss interim compliance issues.
risks.mitigation: Acceptable for most use cases; request SOC 2 reports as interim assurance.

talking_points: GDPR Article 46 requires appropriate safeguards for transfers outside EU
Standard Contractual Clauses are mandatory for non-adequacy jurisdictions
UK Addendum needed post-Brexit for UK data subjects
risk_callouts: Schrems II decision requires transfer impact assessment
US sub-processors may trigger Data Privacy Framework requirements

talking_points: Legal and infosec review requires adequate time
Comparable DPAs offer 45-60 day objection windows
Complex sub-processor security postures need thorough vetting

playbook.fallback: 24 hours with preliminary notice within 12 hours
talking_points: GDPR requires controller notification within 72 hours
Faster processor notification enables timely controller response
Preliminary notification allows proactive incident management
risk_callouts: Ensure notification includes scope, affected data categories, recommended actions

audit.reviewReason: International transfer mechanisms require legal validation
